title: Helix Retail - POC scoping - workload modeling
summary: POC scoping focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling for Helix Retail's checkout recommendation feature. Discussed QPS, concurrency, token distributions, latency SLOs, target benchmarks, and an initial POC timeline. Agreed next steps: provide sample traces, share prompt sets, run synthetic benchmarks with Redwood, and schedule SE-led benchmarking session.
next_steps: Helix: share 2 weeks of anonymized traffic traces and sample prompts (Mike)
Redwood: deliver benchmark plan and infra config for synthetic tests (Priya)
Schedule SE-led benchmark run (30-60m) week of 2025-07-28 (Jordan)
Helix: provision test account and SSO access if needed (Sara)
Both: align on success criteria doc and acceptance thresholds
action_items: Mike Alvarez - Share telemetry (anonymized request/response size + timestamps) - due 2025-07-25
Priya Desai - Produce benchmark config + load script + expected KPIs - due 2025-07-24
Jordan Klein - Schedule benchmark run and send calendar invite - due 2025-07-23
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-07-22 15:00 PT / Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Jordan Klein (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Mike Alvarez (CTO - Helix), Sara Boyd (Eng Manager), Dan Lee (SRE)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, try to keep this focused, we want to lock down QPS/concurrency and success criteria for the POC
[00:08] Mike: cool yeah appreciate it, we have 30 minutes of context then dig into numbers, sorry small on time later so thanks
[00:15] Priya: quick intro, I'm Priya on the SE side, i'll outline what we'll need to size the POC, then we can map to dedicated vs hosted
[00:23] Sara: sounds good. quick note, our main use case is checkout recommendations + post-checkout chat, both are synchronous calls from web clients
[00:33] Dan: and from infra side we care about 95/99 latency, cost and autoscaling behavior - we run on GCP
[00:42] Jordan: perfect. Mike can you give ballpark traffic? qps, concurrency, distribution across endpoints?
[00:48] Mike: sure. baseline daily active users ~120k, peak hourly about 18k concurrent shoppers. For recommendation endpoint expect avg qps 4-6, spike to 12-15 during peaks, per region. Chat is lower qps, ~1-2 average, spikes to 4.
[01:10] Priya: ok so aggregate peak qps around 18-20 across both endpoints or per region?
[01:14] Mike: per region peak is around 12-15 for recommendations, chat adds another 3-4 so total ~15-19 in peak per region. 
[01:24] Priya: good. what's your concurrency model (many short requests vs few long-running)?
[01:28] Sara: recommendations are short request/response - prompt avg input tokens ~90-150 (most ~120), output tokens ~20-40 (usually ~30). chat is longer: input ~200-600 tokens depending on history, output 80-200.
[01:44] Dan: also we run a simple rerank stage: we call a dense embed + rerank flow for top 10 candidates, that adds load for embeddings (batched).
[01:54] Jordan: nice detail. for POC we typically separate the workloads: generation (recommendations/chat) and embedding/rerank. Embeddings can be batched heavily to improve throughput.
[02:04] Priya: couple of clarifying Qs — what's your acceptable latency SLO for recommendations? p95 and p99?
[02:09] Mike: P95 under 250ms is ideal, we can tolerate up to 400ms for P99. For chat, P95 under 600ms and P99 under 1.2s is acceptable since it's interactive but can stream.
[02:23] Priya: good. cost sensitivity?
[02:25] Sara: cost matters but not the primary blocker; reliability and predictable latency are top. We might consider dedicated if it reduces variance.
[02:34] Jordan: that aligns with other customers. for sizing: given avg prompt sizes you mentioned and targeted latency, we'll model QPS and concurrency into required GPU capacity. e.g., for recommendations (avg input 120 tokens + 30 output = 150 tokens total) at 12 qps sustained with concurrency ~40ish (due to client stalls and upstream retries), we estimate needing approximately 1 mid-sized GPU equivalent (this is a rough back-of-envelope).
[02:59] Dan: can you explain concurrency 40 vs qps 12? that seems high
[03:04] Priya: sure — the service concurrency includes queued requests, connections, and inflight KV/cache misses. Web clients hold connections longer and retries multiply inflight. For safety we model concurrency = qps * expected tail latency (in seconds) plus headroom, so at p95 250ms that's 3x, network overhead and retries push it higher.
[03:22] Mike: ok makes sense. what's your approach to benchmark this in the POC?
[03:26] Priya: our benchmark plan has three phases: 1) small functional parity tests (correctness, prompt set pass rates), 2) controlled perf tests (synthetic load to measure throughput and p95/p99 latencies at several qps points), 3) scale/soak test to validate autoscaling and steady-state cost. We'll run both generation and embedding flows.
[03:45] Jordan: we'll want to collect p50/p95/p99 latency, token/sec throughput, GPU utilization, and also accuracy/quality checks compared to your current model. for embeddings rerank we track end-to-end latency and recall metrics.
[03:57] Sara: how long does a typical perf run take?
[04:00] Priya: controlled perf runs 15-30 minutes per QPS point to hit stable metrics; soak runs 2-4 hours depending on what you want to validate. for POC we suggest 1-2 soak runs at peak to validate autoscaling.
[04:11] Dan: on infra side we want observability hooks - can you emit metrics, token-level cost breakdowns and traces?
[04:17] Jordan: yes Redwood Console provides token-level cost, per-route latency, and traces we can hook into your tracing system. we can deliver dashboards for the POC.
[04:27] Mike: cloud region question — we need EU data residency for some traffic, can you run private deployment or VPC?
[04:33] Jordan: yes options: hosted multi-tenant in EU region (with data controls), Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity within customer VPC) or Private on-prem. For POC we usually start with hosted in the target region or dedicated depending on isolation needs.
[04:48] Sara: security checklist — SOC2, encryption at rest, KMS, SSO — we'll need docs
[04:53] Jordan: noted, we'll attach our security pack. Priya can also join security deep-dive if needed.
[04:59] Mike: back to numbers — show me example expected qps vs gpu counts, we need a recommendation for initial reserved capacity for a 4-week POC
[05:06] Priya: rough example: recommendation model (size similar to 3B dense) — at 150 tokens average we can expect per-GPU throughput of ~40-60 rps depending on instance type/quantization. So to hit 12-15 qps sustained you might need 1 GPU for regional serving with autoscaling headroom; for higher peak (x2) plan for 2 GPUs. embeddings are cheap when batched; a single embedding worker can handle high qps with batching (hundreds rps) if latencies allowed.
[05:34] Dan: what about p99 spikes? we need headroom for x2 peaks and network variance
[05:38] Priya: recommend reserve 2 GPUs for the POC with autoscale rules to add burst capacity; that gives you headroom to handle p99 without significant queuing. We can run bench to confirm.
[05:49] Jordan: we'll also run an A/B with smaller quantized model variant as fallback for heavy tail, that helps graceful degradation and cost control.
[05:58] Mike: success criteria for POC? besides latency, what's your recommended acceptance metrics
[06:02] Priya: suggested success criteria: 1) Meet P95/P99 latency targets for 95% of test scenarios, 2) Throughput meets or exceeds sustained qps for recommendation and chat, 3) No functional regressions on the provided prompt set (quality thresholds), 4) Observability and trace integration validated, 5) Cost estimates within agreed budget (within 20% of forecast).
[06:24] Sara: timeline proposal?
[06:26] Jordan: quick plan: this week (by 07/25) Helix shares traces and prompts; Redwood sends benchmark config by 07/24; week of 07/28 run controlled perf tests and a soak; 08/04 analyze results and iterate; POC closeout and decision by 08/15. total ~3 weeks of active testing + analysis.
[06:50] Mike: that timeline works. any blockers from Redwood side?
[06:53] Priya: just sample data and access for synthetic test harness; if you need VPC we may need a slightly longer lead time to provision.
[07:02] Dan: SSO and data handling — i'll send a contact to get SSO set up if we go Dedicated.
[07:07] Jordan: great. one more technical note — for embedding + rerank flows we'll recommend batching window of 10-20ms to keep latency bounded while increasing throughput, and prefix/KV cache for chat to reduce repeat cost.
[07:20] Sara: ok that helps. can you also provide a spreadsheet with cost vs latency tradeoffs?
[07:24] Jordan: yes we'll include a model that maps expected token/sec to cost and latency per model variant.
[07:30] Priya: final recap and owners?
[07:32] Jordan: recap: Helix to share traces/prompts (Mike), Redwood to deliver benchmark plan and run SE-led tests (Priya/Jordan), schedule benchmark week of 07/28. Success criteria as discussed.
[07:45] Mike: thanks all appreciate the clarity, we'll get data by Friday.
[07:50] Jordan: thanks everyone we'll follow up in email with next steps and invites.

Notes: transcription has occasional mislabels and filler words; references to exact GPU types omitted until we profile. Links shared in chat: [Security pack link], [benchmark config template], [sample prompt set].
